h1:
Nakhon Pathom Floating Market Plan
Don Wai – Sampran – Tha Chin Riverside
intro: Nakhon Pathom sits just an hour from Bangkok, but once you cross the Tha Chin River into the Sampran–Nakhon Chai Si side, the mood shifts to a riverside town you can eat your way through all day. We've put together a 2-day floating market plan: wander Don Wai for old-school local food, stop at Sookjai market for organic produce, pay respects at Wat Rai Khing, then take a boat through the pomelo orchards along the Tha Chin. With real opening hours and shops that are actually still running.

blocks.html: What makes the Sampran–Nakhon Chai Si side of Nakhon Pathom special is that it's still a real riverside town, not staged for tourists. Don Wai floating market is an old market on the Tha Chin River where locals actually come to buy their everyday groceries. Sookjai market inside Sampran Riverside is an organic farmers' market where growers bring their own produce to sell. The two have completely different vibes, which is exactly why they pair so well into a single weekend trip.

The key thing that makes this plan click is that Sookjai market only opens on Saturdays and Sundays, and the Wat Rai Khing market only opens on Sundays. So if you want to catch everything, plan your trip across a Saturday and Sunday. We've set Day 1 as Saturday (Don Wai + Sookjai market) and Day 2 as Sunday (Wat Rai Khing + pomelo orchard boat ride).

items: Day 1 (Saturday) — Don Wai floating market mid-morning for braised duck and Thai sweets, then Sookjai market at Sampran Riverside in the afternoon, ending with a riverside café on the Tha Chin
Day 2 (Sunday) — Wat Rai Khing in the morning, a stroll through the riverside market, then a late-morning boat ride through the Nakhon Chai Si pomelo orchards, with a riverside café on the way back
Distances — every stop is within a 15 km radius, with 10–20 min drives between them. Best done with your own car or a rental

blocks.html: The first day is all about eating and market-hopping. Start at Don Wai floating market mid-morning when the stalls are fully stocked, then move on to Sookjai market in the afternoon. The two are only about 10 km apart.

items.note: If you're driving, take Phetkasem or Borommaratchachonnani Road — it's about an hour either way
Open 07:00–18:30 on weekends, with more stalls than on weekdays. You can park inside Wat Don Wai

items.activity: Braised duck at Nai Nub + palm cake from Pa Khai
items.note: The braised duck is a market favorite, and there are several stalls selling old-style Thai sweets. Come hungry

items.activity: Boat ride on the Tha Chin in front of the market
items.note: There are boats for short riverside cruises, roughly ฿40–60 per person per round. Ask at the pier in front of the market

items.activity: Move on to Sookjai market, Sampran Riverside
items.note: Organic farmers' market, open weekends only, around 08:00–15:00. Arrive before 3pm to catch the fresh produce

items.activity: Shop for organic vegetables, rice, and Thai sweets
items.note: Farmers sell their own produce, so it's great for picking up unusual souvenirs

items.activity: Relax at a Tha Chin riverside café for the evening breeze
items.note: The Nakhon Chai Si area has several riverside cafés — pick one along the way back to your hotel

blocks.title: Timing tip
blocks.html: On weekdays Don Wai has fewer stalls and shops close early, while Sookjai market only opens on weekends. If you come on a weekday you'll only get a quiet Don Wai and nothing else. For the lively atmosphere, aim for Saturday or Sunday.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Wat Rai Khing + pomelo orchard boat ride

blocks.html: Day two starts a little later with a visit to Wat Rai Khing, a royal temple on the Tha Chin River that locals in Nakhon Pathom hold dear. Then comes something you can't easily do in Bangkok: a boat ride into the pomelo orchards of Nakhon Chai Si, the province's famous pomelo country.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Sunday · Tha Chin riverside, Nakhon Chai Si

items.activity: Pay respects at Wat Rai Khing
items.note: Pay your respects to Luang Pho Wat Rai Khing, an important Buddha image for the province. The temple sits right on the Tha Chin, with a pleasant riverside walk

items.activity: Browse the Wat Rai Khing market
items.note: A community market across from the temple, open Sundays only from morning to noon, packed with breakfast eats

items.activity: Drive to the Nakhon Chai Si pomelo orchards
items.note: Such as Suan Thai Thawi, which has grown pomelos for over 50 years. Call ahead to book before you go

items.activity: Boat ride through the pomelo orchard + pick pomelos
items.note: Take a boat into the riverside orchard, learn how pomelos are harvested, and rest at the small café inside the orchard
Restaurants along the Tha Chin near Nakhon Chai Si serve fresh freshwater fish and river prawns, priced by the dish

items.activity: Wrap up the trip at a riverside café
items.note: Sip coffee and watch the boats go by before driving back to Bangkok in the early evening to dodge the traffic

blocks.html: The fun of a floating market trip is the food. We've picked the standout dishes at each stop along the route, ranked by how often locals here talk about them.

items.name: Nai Nub braised duck (Don Wai)
items.blurb: A long-running braised duck shop at Don Wai market. The duck is tender and the braising broth is fragrant with spices — it's the dish almost every table at Don Wai orders.

items.name: Pa Khai palm cake (Don Wai)
items.blurb: Soft, fragrant steamed palm cake — an old-style Thai sweet that's getting harder to find. Pa Khai has been making it at the market for years, and it travels well as a souvenir.

items.name: Organic vegetables and rice (Sookjai market)
items.blurb: Farmers sell their own fresh vegetables, pesticide-free fruit, eggs, mushrooms, and organic rice at fair prices — great to take home for cooking.

items.name: Nakhon Chai Si pomelo
items.blurb: Khao Nam Phueng and Thong Dee varieties with crisp, juicy flesh that's sweet with a touch of tart — famous across the province. Bought fresh from a riverside orchard, it tastes better than what you'll find in town.
items.meta: Nakhon Chai Si pomelo orchards · seasonal

items.name: Tha Chin river fish and prawns
items.blurb: Riverside restaurants around Nakhon Chai Si serve fresh freshwater fish, grilled river prawns, and clown knifefish cakes — perfect with the riverside setting.

items.name: Tha Chin riverside café coffee
items.blurb: Riverside cafés along the Nakhon Chai Si in renovated old warehouses, where you can sit in the breeze and watch boats pass. Some you reach by boat — a relaxed way to end the trip.

blocks.text: Where to stay and getting around

blocks.html: If you'd rather not drive back to Bangkok at night, staying a night on the Sampran–Nakhon Chai Si side is easier. You can wake up early for Wat Rai Khing and catch the Sunday market right on time.

items.name: Stay at Sampran Riverside
items.blurb: There are riverside resorts within the Sampran Riverside grounds, an easy walk to Sookjai market — good for a family trip.

items.name: Stay in Nakhon Pathom town
items.blurb: If you want to be near Phra Pathom Chedi and the food in town, stay in the town center and drive out to the Sampran side, about 20–30 min away.

blocks.title: Getting around
blocks.html: This route is easiest with your own car or a rental, since the stops are spread along the Tha Chin and there's no direct public transport linking them. Without a car, you can use local taxis or hired vehicles for individual legs, but it's best to arrange pickup times in advance.

faq.q: What days and hours is Don Wai floating market open?
faq.a: Don Wai floating market is open every day — roughly 08:00–17:00 Monday to Friday, and 07:00–18:30 on Saturdays and Sundays. On weekends more shops open and there's more on offer, while weekdays are quiet with fewer stalls.

faq.q: Is Sookjai market at Sampran Riverside open every day?
faq.a: No. Sookjai is an organic farmers' market open on Saturdays and Sundays only, roughly 08:00–15:00. Come before the afternoon to catch the fresh produce. It's closed on weekdays.

faq.q: How many days do you need for this route?
faq.a: 2 days and 1 night is just right. Day one covers Don Wai and Sookjai market, and day two covers Wat Rai Khing and the pomelo orchard boat ride. If you only have one day, focus mainly on Don Wai + Wat Rai Khing.

faq.q: What day is the Wat Rai Khing market open?
faq.a: The community market across from Wat Rai Khing opens on Sundays only, from morning until around noon — which is why it works well as the morning stop on day two of this plan.

Not at all. The Sampran–Nakhon Chai Si side is about an hour from Bangkok by car, and all the stops are within a 15 km radius with 10–20 min drives between them. It's perfect for a weekend trip that doesn't take much planning.
